The Golden Age of Animation: Exploring the Best 90s Animated Movies

Discover the magic of 90s animated movies! From Disney classics to Pixar's CGI revolution, our top 10 list showcases the decade's best. Relive the nostalgia with The Lion King, Toy Story, and hidden gems that defined a golden era of animation.

23 September 2024 · RewindZone Archive

As a passionate chronicler of 90s nostalgia at Rewind Zone, I've always held a special place in my heart for the animated films of that decade. The 1990s marked a pivotal moment in the history of animation, ushering in a new era of creativity, technological innovation, and storytelling. This decade saw the birth of computer-generated imagery (CGI) and produced some of the most beloved animated films of all time. Join me as we dive into the world of 90s animated movies, exploring their impact, diversity, and enduring legacy.

The Rise of CGI and Its Impact on 90s Animation

The introduction of CGI technology in the 1990s revolutionised the animation industry. This new tool allowed animators to create visually stunning worlds and characters that were previously impossible with traditional hand-drawn techniques. The release of Pixar's Toy Story in 1995 marked a significant milestone, being the first fully computer-animated feature film.

However, the 90s weren't just about CGI. This decade saw a beautiful blend of traditional hand-drawn animation, stop-motion, and computer-generated imagery, resulting in a diverse range of visual styles and storytelling techniques.

Let's dive straight in with my Top 10:

This list represents what I consider to be the cream of the crop in 90s animation. It includes a mix of Disney classics, pioneering CGI works, and some less mainstream choices that I believe truly showcase the diverse range of animated films that made the 1990s so special.

At the top of my list, The Lion King and Toy Story stand as towering achievements in traditional and computer animation, respectively. These films not only pushed the boundaries of what was possible in animation but also told timeless stories that continue to resonate with audiences today.

I've placed Princess Mononoke at number 4 because I believe it represents the growing influence and artistry of anime during this period. Its complex themes and stunning visuals make it a standout not just in anime, but in animation as a whole.

The inclusion of The Iron Giant and The Prince of Egypt on this list underscores the quality of non-Disney animated features produced during this decade. These films proved that compelling storytelling and beautiful animation weren't exclusive to the House of Mouse.

I've also included FernGully: The Last Rainforest, a film that might not always make it onto "best of" lists, but one that I believe deserves recognition for its environmental themes and charming execution (and the mastery of Robin Williams).

On that note, you can watch the full movie on YouTube below and judge for yourselves.

The Nightmare Before Christmas earns its place on this list for its innovative stop-motion animation and its delightfully dark yet whimsical story. In a decade dominated by traditional 2D and emerging 3D techniques, this film stands out as a testament to the enduring appeal of stop-motion.

Beyond Disney: The Diversity of 90s Animation

Advertisement

While Disney dominated much of the animated landscape in the 1990s, the decade also saw remarkable contributions from other studios and countries. Some notable examples include:

  • Studio Ghibli's Princess Mononoke , Porco Rosso and Whisper of the Heart
  • Warner Bros.' The Iron Giant
  • Don Bluth's Anastasia
  • DreamWorks' The Prince of Egypt and Antz

The inclusion of anime films like Ghost in the Shell (1995) in discussions about influential 90s animations showcases the global nature of the medium's evolution during this period.

Hidden Gems: Lesser-Known 90s Animated Films

While blockbusters from major studios often dominate discussions about 90s animation, the decade produced many lesser-known gems that deserve recognition. These films showcase the diversity of stories, styles, and themes explored in animated cinema during this era:

  • FernGully: The Last Rainforest (1992) - This environmentally-themed film set in an Australian rainforest features fairies fighting to save their home from pollution and deforestation.
  • The Swan Princess (1994) - A musical adaptation of the ballet "Swan Lake," this film offers a fresh take on the classic tale with memorable characters and songs.
  • Balto (1995) - Based on the true story of a sled dog who helped save children from a diphtheria epidemic, this adventure film combines historical elements with animated storytelling.
  • Cats Don't Dance (1997) - This musical comedy about a cat trying to make it big in Hollywood serves as a clever allegory for the struggles of minorities in the entertainment industry.
  • The Thief and the Cobbler (1993) - Famous for its troubled production history, this film gained a cult following for its unique and intricate animation style.
  • Once Upon a Forest (1993) - An environmental fable about woodland creatures trying to save their forest home, this film tackles ecological themes in a way accessible to young audiences.
  • The Pagemaster (1994) - Combining live-action and animation, this adventure set in a library celebrates the power of books and imagination.
  • Rover Dangerfield (1991) - Featuring the voice of comedian Rodney Dangerfield, this comedy follows the adventures of a Las Vegas show dog adjusting to farm life.

These lesser-known films demonstrate the breadth of creativity in 90s animation beyond the major studio releases, offering unique stories and visual styles that enriched the animated landscape of the decade.

Animated Films with Mature Themes

The 1990s also saw a trend towards animated films that tackled more mature themes and darker subject matter. Films like The Nightmare Before Christmas (1993), Princess Mononoke (1997), Batman: Mask of the Phantasm (1993), and previously mentioned Ghost in the Shell (1995) pushed the boundaries of what animated films could explore, appealing to older audiences and cementing animation as a medium capable of profound storytelling.

The 1990s truly represented a golden age for animation, marked by technological advancements, diverse storytelling, and films that continue to captivate audiences of all ages. From the hand-drawn majesty of Disney's renaissance to the CGI revolution led by Pixar, and the mature themes explored in anime and independent productions, 90s animated movies laid the foundation for the vibrant and varied animation landscape we enjoy today.

As a fan and chronicler of 90s pop culture, I can confidently say that the animated films of this decade hold a special place in the hearts of many. They represent a time of incredible creativity and innovation in the world of animation, and their influence continues to be felt in the industry today. So, the next time you're in the mood for some nostalgic viewing, why not revisit one of these 90s animated classics? You might just find yourself rediscovering the magic that made this era so special.
